A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CaMKII-alphaB is a critical mediator of the apoptotic cascade induced by NMDA.
AIP inhibits CaMKII, which in turn blocks the up-regulation of the apoptosis-associated genes and thus protects against NMDA-induced cell death.
CaMKII is involved in the regulation of the expression of genes associated with cell survival and death in the retina and that CaMKII inhibitors may be used in the treatment of retinal diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the CaMKII inhibitor AIP, which we developed, protects retinal neurons against NMDA-induced cell death and that the protective effects of AIP are associated with a down regulation of the expression of apoptosis-associated genes in these neurons.
AIP can protect against retinal damage by inhibiting the expression of apoptosis-associated genes.
